[[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! revision.text:
[[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! revision.text:
[[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! revision.text:
[[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! revision.text:
[[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! revision.text:
[[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" !
