[[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft|12=draft}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft|12=draft}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft|12=draft}}. The list is ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft|12=draft}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft|12=draft}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft|12=draft}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft|12=draft}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[ファイル:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|[[大仙陵古墳]]は、日本最大の古墳にして[[前方後円墳]]の代表例。[[宮内庁]]は{{ruby|百舌鳥耳原中陵|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}}と呼び、[[仁徳天皇]]の[[陵墓]]（別名：仁徳天皇陵）と{{ruby|治定|じじょう}}している。
画像（2007年撮影）
{{国土航空写真}}。]] '''日本の大規模古墳一覧'''（にほん の だいきぼこ ふん いちらん）では、[[古墳時代]]の[[日本列島]]で造営された大規模な[[古墳]]を一覧形式で記載する。墳丘長を基準としてランキングし、墳丘長200[[メートル]]以上のものだけを扱う。 なお、全長120メートル以上の古墳の[[都道府県]]別の分布などの表も合わせて記載する。 == 全長200メートル以上の大規模古墳一覧 == 以下に示す表は、[[白石太一郎]]の原表をもとに、[[和田萃]]（1992）{{Sfn|和田萃|1992}}、[[広瀬和雄]]（2003）{{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}などを参照して作成したものである。陵墓の治定は[[宮内庁]]によるもので、当該人物が実際にその古墳に被葬されているかどうかを示すものではない。また、備考に掲げた「古墳群」「古墳集団」の範疇は、その多くを和田（1992）に拠っている。 古墳時代の日本列島で造営された200メートル以上の巨大古墳は、下記のとおり全部で37基である。いずれも、王・[[大王 (ヤマト王権)|大王]]級の[[首長]]の墳墓と考えられるが、[[大阪府]][[羽曳野市]]の[[墓山古墳]]（第23位）は同市に所在する[[誉田御廟山古墳]]（第2位）の[[陪塚]]である。 {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" !順位||古墳名||||所在地||旧国||||時代||時期||期||||墳丘長（m）||||高さ（m）||||治定陵墓名||備考 |- |1||[[大仙陵古墳|大仙陵古墳

*「'''時代'''」は[[白石太一郎]]の原表によった。前期・中期・後期の3区分は慣用的に使用されており、それぞれ'''前期'''（3世紀中ごろから4世紀後半）、'''中期'''（4世紀末から5世紀後半）、'''後期'''（5世紀末から6世紀末）に相当する。「'''時期'''」は和田萃（1992）{{Sfn|和田萃|1992}}その他 URL なども参照して充当した暦年代である。「時代」と「時期」は研究者の編年観の相違により若干の食い違いがみられる。これ以外に、[[広瀬和雄]]の10期編年を掲げた。それが「'''期'''」である。10期編年と慣用的3区分の関係は、1-4期が前期、5-7期が中期、8-10期が後期に相当する。広瀬（2003）による言及のない古墳については空欄とした。広瀬の10期編年の暦年代を以下に記す。 ::'''1期'''（3世紀中ごろ-3世紀後半ごろ）、'''2期'''（3世紀末ごろ-4世紀初めごろ）、'''3期'''（4世紀前半ごろ-4世紀中ごろ）、'''4期'''（4世紀後半ごろ）、'''5期'''（4世紀末ごろ-5世紀初めごろにかけて）、'''6期'''（5世紀前半ごろ）、'''7期'''（5世紀中ごろ-5世紀後半ごろ）、'''8期'''（5世紀末ごろ-6世紀初めごろ）、'''9期'''（6世紀前半ごろ-6世紀中ごろ）、'''10期'''（6世紀後半ごろ-7世紀初めごろ）。 news |和書 |date=2000-05-19 |title=（※記事名：無記）|url= |publisher=奈良新聞社 |newspaper=[[奈良新聞]] |accessdate=2020-02-20 }}{{出典無効|date=2020年2月20日|title=情報不足。}}。 === 補説1 === 古墳時代における日本列島の首長墓・王墓は、[[前方後円墳]]、[[前方後方墳]]、[[円墳]]、[[方墳]]など同時代の同一地域において多様な墳形が並存しており、その点で同じ時代の[[朝鮮半島]]の首長墓・王墓とは著しい対照をなしている。 上に掲げた37基の古墳の形状は、すべて[[前方後円墳]]である。 [[広瀬和雄]]によれば、おおむね前方後円墳、前方後方墳、円墳、方墳の順に優位性をあらわす墳形秩序をもっていた{{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003|p=132}}としており、このことより、上記の墳丘長200メートルを超える大規模な前方後円墳は「大王級の首長の墓」とみなされていたことがわかる。全長200メートル超の古墳の分布は、岡山県の2基、群馬県、京都府の各1基の計5基を除くとすべて大阪・奈良の2府県に集中しており、大阪府下では太田茶臼山古墳（第20位）が令制の摂津国に属するほかは、すべて河内国・和泉国に分布する。すなわち、[[大阪平野]]のなかでも[[大和川]]流域の南部に濃密な分布傾向を示している。 前方後円墳は、3世紀中葉の日本列島で生まれた古墳形式である。3世紀から7世紀初頭にいたるまで、約5,200基造営されたといわれるが、前方後円墳の特質として広瀬和雄は、全体における可視性、形状における画一性、墳丘規模における階層性の3点を掲げている{{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003|p=7}}。 なかでも、大仙古墳と誉田御廟山古墳は、中国の[[秦]]代における[[始皇帝陵]]（[[中華人民共和国]][[陝西省]][[西安市]]郊外）と並んで世界最大規模を有する陵墓である。朝鮮半島最大の古墳が、5世紀代後半の[[新羅]]の双円墳[[皇南大塚古墳]]（[[大韓民国]][[慶州市]]）であり、その墳丘長が約120メートルであることからも、日本列島で造営された古墳がいかに大規模なものが多かったかがわかる。そのいっぽうで、広瀬の指摘した前方後円墳の規模の階層性を考慮すると、古墳時代の日本では、規模それ自体が重要な政治的意味を有していたと推定できる。 表より、古墳時代の日本列島では墳丘長120メートル以上の古墳が132(+1)基もつくられ、そのうちの過半数が大阪府と奈良県、つまりヤマトの支配地域に分布していることがわかる。ヤマトに次いで大規模な古墳が数多く作られたのは吉備であり、全国で4番目に大きい造山古墳が吉備で最も巨大な古墳である。また規模の点において、ヤマトと吉備の支配地域の古墳が全国第45位までを占めており、[[ヤマト政権]]と[[吉備政権]]の盛強を物語る。そのいっぽうで大規模古墳は、同じ地方でも多数つくられた地域、ほとんどつくられなかった地域があり、偏在傾向が指摘できる。 墳形の面でみてゆくと、総計132基のうち、前方後円墳が128基、[[前方後方墳]]が4基である。このことより、前方後円墳は大王および地方の王の墓として卓越した地位をあたえられていたことがわかる。前方後方墳もまた同様であるが、年代的には前期に偏っており、両者の墳形の違いはヤマトを中心とする畿内王権との関係の相違などによることが示唆される{{Refnest|group="注"|都出比呂志や白石太一郎は、[[卑弥呼]]晩年における[[邪馬台国]]と[[狗奴国]]の抗争と後円墳祖形と後方墳祖形の分布の偏在との関連を指摘している。{{Sfn|都出比呂志|2000|pp=12-13}}}}。全長120メートル以上の前方後方墳4基はいずれも前期の大和（奈良県）の古墳である。前方後方墳は、日本列島全体からすれば、前期・中期に築造されたものが多く、[[長崎島県]]から[[宮城県]]までの各地域に分布するが、とくに[[島根県]]東部の意宇平野、北陸の[[加賀]]・[[能登]]地方、[[濃尾平野]]や[[関東地方]]のとくに[[那須]]地方などに多い。前期後半から中期以降（4世紀後半以降）は、前方後方墳の造営が激減し、以前にもまして前方後円墳が畿内の王あるいは各地の地域政権の王として定型化していったものと思われる。 なお、前方後円墳は[[韓国]]の[[栄山江]]流域を中心に[[全羅道]]地方から13基が見つかっており、年代的には5世紀後半から6世紀初めにかけてに多く位置づけられる。 === 補説2 === 『前方後円墳集成』によれば、100メートルを超える古墳は303基におよんでいる。墳形の内訳は前方後円墳が291基、前方後方墳が11基、円墳が1基である。築造時期では前期112基、中期93基、後期57基となっている{{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003|pp=136-139}}※原出典は{{Harvnb|『前方後円墳集成 ???編』|1992|p=}} {{要ページ番号|date=2020年2月20日}}{{出典無効|date=2020年2月20日|title=特定する為の情報を欠く。}} ほか。。地域別では、大和73基（24.2[[パーセント|%]]）、河内30基（9.9%）、和泉14基（4.6%）、[[山城国|山城]]12基（4.0%）、摂津11基（3.6%）、上野27基（8.9%）、[[下総]]15基（5.0%）、武蔵10基（3.3%）、吉備13基（4.3%）、日向12基（4.0%）などとなっている。[[畿内]]全域では140基であり、46.2%を占め、全体の半数近い割合となっている。また、上位10国・地域で204基で67.3%に及び、それ以外に2桁におよぶ地域はない。 上表は、5世紀代を中心にした周辺諸国との国際比較である。ヤマト王権においては、墳丘の規模が重大な意味をもっていたことがうかがえるとともに、広瀬和雄が指摘する「見せる王権としての可視性」が随所に確認できる。なお、中国の[[魏晋南北朝時代]]の王墓では南北の地域差が顕著であり、[[黄河]]流域の北部では方丘墓が主流であるのに対し、[[長江]]流域の南部では円丘墓の[[伝統]]があってさかんに造営されていたことが知られている{{Sfn|都出比呂志|2000|pp=66-67}}。 *「'''時代'''」は[[白石太一郎]]の原表によった。前期・中期・後期の3区分は慣用的に使用されており、それぞれ'''前期'''（3世紀中ごろから4世紀後半）、'''中期'''（4世紀末から5世紀後半）、'''後期'''（5世紀末から6世紀末）に相当する。「'''時期'''」は和田萃（1992）{{Sfn|和田萃|1992}}その他 URL なども参照して充当した暦年代である。「時代」と「時期」は研究者の編年観の相違により若干の食い違いがみられる。これ以外に、[[広瀬和雄]]の10期編年を掲げた。それが「'''期'''」である。10期編年と慣用的3区分の関係は、1-4期が前期、5-7期が中期、8-10期が後期に相当する。広瀬（2003）による言及のない古墳については空欄とした。広瀬の10期編年の暦年代を以下に記す。 ::'''1期'''（3世紀中ごろ-3世紀後半ごろ）、'''2期'''（3世紀末ごろ-4世紀初めごろ）、'''3期'''（4世紀前半ごろ-4世紀中ごろ）、'''4期'''（4世紀後半ごろ）、'''5期'''（4世紀末ごろ-5世紀初めごろにかけて）、'''6期'''（5世紀前半ごろ）、'''7期'''（5世紀中ごろ-5世紀後半ごろ）、'''8期'''（5世紀末ごろ-6世紀初めごろ）、'''9期'''（6世紀前半ごろ-6世紀中ごろ）、'''10期'''（6世紀後半ごろ-7世紀初めごろ）。 * ※島の山古墳は、1996年度の[[橿原考古学研究所]]の[[発掘調査]]では全長190メートルとされた現地説明会資料[http://www.kashikoken.jp/from-site/sima.htm]{{リンク切れ|date=2020年2月20日}}{{出典無効|date=2020年2月20日|title=直接リンク禁止、情報不足。}}が、その後の精査により墳丘全長200メートル以上におよぶ規模であることが確認された{{Cite news |和書 |date=2000-05-19 |title=（※記事名：無記）|url= |publisher=奈良新聞社 |newspaper=[[奈良新聞]] |accessdate=2020-02-20 }}{{出典無効|date=2020年2月20日|title=情報不足。}}。 === 補説1 === 古墳時代における日本列島の首長墓・王墓は、[[前方後円墳]]、[[前方後方墳]]、[[円墳]]、[[方墳]]など同時代の同一地域において多様な墳形が並存しており、その点で同じ時代の[[朝鮮半島]]の首長墓・王墓とは著しい対照をなしている。 上に掲げた37基の古墳の形状は、すべて[[前方後円墳]]である。 [[広瀬和雄]]によれば、おおむね前方後円墳、前方後方墳、円墳、方墳の順に優位性をあらわす墳形秩序をもっていた{{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003|p=132}}としており、このことより、上記の墳丘長200メートルを超える大規模な前方後円墳は「大王級の首長の墓」とみなされていたことがわかる。全長200メートル超の古墳の分布は、岡山県の2基、群馬県、京都府の各1基の計5基を除くとすべて大阪・奈良の2府県に集中しており、大阪府下では太田茶臼山古墳（第20位）が令制の摂津国に属するほかは、すべて河内国・和泉国に分布する。すなわち、[[大阪平野]]のなかでも[[大和川]]流域の南部に濃密な分布傾向を示している。 前方後円墳は、3世紀中葉の日本列島で生まれた古墳形式である。3世紀から7世紀初頭にいたるまで、約5,200基造営されたといわれるが、前方後円墳の特質として広瀬和雄は、全体における可視性、形状における画一性、墳丘規模における階層性の3点を掲げている{{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003|p=7}}。 なかでも、大仙古墳と誉田御廟山古墳は、中国の[[秦]]代における[[始皇帝陵]]（[[中華人民共和国]][[陝西省]][[西安市]]郊外）と並んで世界最大規模を有する陵墓である。朝鮮半島最大の古墳が、5世紀代後半の[[新羅]]の双円墳[[皇南大塚古墳]]（[[大韓民国]][[慶州市]]）であり、その墳丘長が約120メートルであることからも、日本列島で造営された古墳がいかに大規模なものが多かったかがわかる。そのいっぽうで、広瀬の指摘した前方後円墳の規模の階層性を考慮すると、古墳時代の日本では、規模それ自体が重要な政治的意味を有していたと推定できる。 表より、古墳時代の日本列島では墳丘長120メートル以上の古墳が132(+1)基もつくられ、そのうちの過半数が大阪府と奈良県、つまりヤマトの支配地域に分布していることがわかる。ヤマトに次いで大規模な古墳が数多く作られたのは吉備であり、全国で4番目に大きい造山古墳が吉備で最も巨大な古墳である。また規模の点において、ヤマトと吉備の支配地域の古墳が全国第45位までを占めており、[[ヤマト政権]]と[[吉備政権]]の盛強を物語る。そのいっぽうで大規模古墳は、同じ地方でも多数つくられた地域、ほとんどつくられなかった地域があり、偏在傾向が指摘できる。 墳形の面でみてゆくと、総計132基のうち、前方後円墳が128基、[[前方後方墳]]が4基である。このことより、前方後円墳は大王および地方の王の墓として卓越した地位をあたえられていたことがわかる。前方後方墳もまた同様であるが、年代的には前期に偏っており、両者の墳形の違いはヤマトを中心とする畿内王権との関係の相違などによることが示唆される{{Refnest|group="注"|都出比呂志や白石太一郎は、[[卑弥呼]]晩年における[[邪馬台国]]と[[狗奴国]]の抗争と後円墳祖形と後方墳祖形の分布の偏在との関連を指摘している。{{Sfn|都出比呂志|2000|pp=12-13}}}}。全長120メートル以上の前方後方墳4基はいずれも前期の大和（奈良県）の古墳である。前方後方墳は、日本列島全体からすれば、前期・中期に築造されたものが多く、[[長崎島県]]から[[宮城県]]までの各地域に分布するが、とくに[[島根県]]東部の意宇平野、北陸の[[加賀]]・[[能登]]地方、[[濃尾平野]]や[[関東地方]]のとくに[[那須]]地方などに多い。前期後半から中期以降（4世紀後半以降）は、前方後方墳の造営が激減し、以前にもまして前方後円墳が畿内の王あるいは各地の地域政権の王として定型化していったものと思われる。 なお、前方後円墳は[[韓国]]の[[栄山江]]流域を中心に[[全羅道]]地方から13基が見つかっており、年代的には5世紀後半から6世紀初めにかけてに多く位置づけられる。 === 補説2 === 『前方後円墳集成』によれば、100メートルを超える古墳は303基におよんでいる。墳形の内訳は前方後円墳が291基、前方後方墳が11基、円墳が1基である。築造時期では前期112基、中期93基、後期57基となっている{{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003|pp=136-139}}※原出典は{{Harvnb|『前方後円墳集成 ???編』|1992|p=}} {{要ページ番号|date=2020年2月20日}}{{出典無効|date=2020年2月20日|title=特定する為の情報を欠く。}} ほか。。地域別では、大和73基（24.2[[パーセント|%]]）、河内30基（9.9%）、和泉14基（4.6%）、[[山城国|山城]]12基（4.0%）、摂津11基（3.6%）、上野27基（8.9%）、[[下総]]15基（5.0%）、武蔵10基（3.3%）、吉備13基（4.3%）、日向12基（4.0%）などとなっている。[[畿内]]全域では140基であり、46.2%を占め、全体の半数近い割合となっている。また、上位10国・地域で204基で67.3%に及び、それ以外に2桁におよぶ地域はない。 == 墳丘要素の国際比較 == {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: left;font-size:small" !要素||[[倭国]]||[[新羅]]||[[伽耶]]||[[百済]]||[[高句麗]] |- |墳形||前方後円墳、前方後方墳、円墳、
方墳、造り出し付き円墳など||円墳、一部に[[双円墳]]||円墳||円墳||方墳 |- |墳丘規模||最大525メートル||最大120メートル||10-30メートル||10-30メートル||最大63メートル |- |[[周濠]]||一重、二重、外堤||なし||なし||なし||なし |- |[[陪塚]]||衛星型など||なし||なし||なし||なし |- |外部の装飾||[[円筒埴輪]]列、壺形埴輪列、[[段築]]、[[葺石]]||基本的になし||基本的になし||基本的になし||基本的になし（[[積石塚]]の伝統あり） |- |} 上表は、5世紀代を中心にした周辺諸国との国際比較である。ヤマト王権においては、墳丘の規模が重大な意味をもっていたことがうかがえるとともに、広瀬和雄が指摘する「見せる王権としての可視性」が随所に確認できる。なお、中国の[[魏晋南北朝時代]]の王墓では南北の地域差が顕著であり、[[黄河]]流域の北部では方丘墓が主流であるのに対し、[[長江]]流域の南部では円丘墓の[[伝統]]があってさかんに造営されていたことが知られている{{Sfn|都出比呂志|2000|pp=66-67}}。 [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|12=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|12=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|12=draft}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|12=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|12=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=draft}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=draft}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Nintoku|qq=}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese archipelago|qq=}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Kings (Yamato court)|qq=}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Habikino|qq=}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Nintoku|qq=}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese archipelago|qq=}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Kings (Yamato court)|qq=}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Habikino|qq=}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Nintoku|qq=}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese archipelago|qq=}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Kings (Yamato court)|qq=}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Habikino|qq=}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Nintoku|qq=}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese archipelago|qq=}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Kings (Yamato court)|qq=}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Habikino|qq=}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" !
