[[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Nintoku|qq=}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese archipelago|qq=}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Kings (Yamato court)|qq=}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Habikino|qq=}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Nintoku|qq=}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese archipelago|qq=}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Kings (Yamato court)|qq=}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Habikino|qq=}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! Shiraishi's classification. The three conventional subdivisions—Early (mid-3rd century to late 4th century), Middle (late 4th century to late 5th century), and Late (late 5th century to late 6th century)—are noted. The specific chronological periods are based on Wada (1992) and other sources. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} * {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} * {{ill|Yamato Court|ja|ヤマト王権|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Court|qq=}} * {{ill|List of kofun in Japan|ja|日本の古墳一覧|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of kofun in Japan|qq=}} * {{ill|Royal tombs|ja|大王墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Royal tombs|qq=}} == External Links == * {{Cite web|title=Japan's Kofun: "100 Largest Kofun in Japan" |url=http://www.asuka-tobira.com/kofun/kofun.html#100 |website=Asuka no Tobira |accessdate=2020-02-20}} * {{Cite web|title=Research on Zenpō-kōen-fun in Jeollado, Korea |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/wfsection/article.php?articleid=44 |website=Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program |accessdate=2020-02-20}} {{translated page|ja|日本の大規模古墳一覧|version=100010673|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Lists of kofun in Japan|Large-scale]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:List of large kofun in Japan]] }} [[sn:List of large kofun in Japan]] [[ja:%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC%E3%81%AE%E5%A4%A7%E8%A6%8F%E6%A8%A1%E5%8F%A4%E5%A2%B3%E4%B8%80%E8%A6%A7]] [[en:List of large kofun in Japan]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

[[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Nintoku|qq=}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese archipelago|qq=}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Kings (Yamato court)|qq=}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Habikino|qq=}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Nintoku|qq=}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese archipelago|qq=}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Kings (Yamato court)|qq=}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Habikino|qq=}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! Shiraishi's classification. The three conventional subdivisions—Early (mid-3rd century to late 4th century), Middle (late 4th century to late 5th century), and Late (late 5th century to late 6th century)—are noted. The specific chronological periods are based on Wada (1992) and other sources. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} * {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} * {{ill|Yamato Court|ja|ヤマト王権|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Court|qq=}} * {{ill|List of kofun in Japan|ja|日本の古墳一覧|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of kofun in Japan|qq=}} * {{ill|Royal tombs|ja|大王墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Royal tombs|qq=}} == External Links == * {{Cite web|title=Japan's Kofun: "100 Largest Kofun in Japan" |url=http://www.asuka-tobira.com/kofun/kofun.html#100 |website=Asuka no Tobira |accessdate=2020-02-20}} * {{Cite web|title=Research on Zenpō-kōen-fun in Jeollado, Korea |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/wfsection/article.php?articleid=44 |website=Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program |accessdate=2020-02-20}} {{translated page|ja|日本の大規模古墳一覧|version=100010673|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Lists of kofun in Japan|Large-scale]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:List of large kofun in Japan]] }} [[sn:List of large kofun in Japan]] [[ja:%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC%E3%81%AE%E5%A4%A7%E8%A6%8F%E6%A8%A1%E5%8F%A4%E5%A2%B3%E4%B8%80%E8%A6%A7]] [[en:List of large kofun in Japan]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

[[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Nintoku|qq=}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese archipelago|qq=}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Kings (Yamato court)|qq=}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Habikino|qq=}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Nintoku|qq=}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|ja|日本列島|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese archipelago|qq=}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Household Agency|qq=}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Great Kings (Yamato court)|ja|大王 (ヤマト王権)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Kings (Yamato court)|qq=}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|ja|羽曳野市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Habikino|qq=}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! Shiraishi's classification. The three conventional subdivisions—Early (mid-3rd century to late 4th century), Middle (late 4th century to late 5th century), and Late (late 5th century to late 6th century)—are noted. The specific chronological periods are based on Wada (1992) and other sources. == References == {{Reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Kofun|ja|古墳|1=Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun|qq=}} * {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kofun period|qq=}} * {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳|lt=Zenpokoenfun|comement=second one attempting to fix this error|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|comment=doing this because I need to differentiate it in piped links too with my new interwiki tool as not the ambiguous phrase keyhole shaped kofun|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpō-kōen-fun|13=User:Immanuelle/Zenpokoenfun|qq=}} * {{ill|Yamato Court|ja|ヤマト王権|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamato Court|qq=}} * {{ill|List of kofun in Japan|ja|日本の古墳一覧|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of kofun in Japan|qq=}} * {{ill|Royal tombs|ja|大王墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Royal tombs|qq=}} == External Links == * {{Cite web|title=Japan's Kofun: "100 Largest Kofun in Japan" |url=http://www.asuka-tobira.com/kofun/kofun.html#100 |website=Asuka no Tobira |accessdate=2020-02-20}} * {{Cite web|title=Research on Zenpō-kōen-fun in Jeollado, Korea |url=http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/modules/wfsection/article.php?articleid=44 |website=Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program |accessdate=2020-02-20}} {{translated page|ja|日本の大規模古墳一覧|version=100010673|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Lists of kofun in Japan|Large-scale]] [[Category:Completion tier 6]] [[Category:List of large kofun in Japan]] }} [[sn:List of large kofun in Japan]] [[ja:%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC%E3%81%AE%E5%A4%A7%E8%A6%8F%E6%A8%A1%E5%8F%A4%E5%A2%B3%E4%B8%80%E8%A6%A7]] [[en:List of large kofun in Japan]] [[ja:&action=edit]]

[[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! revision.text:
[[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:56, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:56, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:56, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:56, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:56, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11505891]] Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:20, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:56, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11505891]] Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:20, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:56, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11505891]] Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:20, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:56, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q11505891]] Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 05:20, 12 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry (none) Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:56, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of [[:en:Emperor Nintoku|Emperor Nintoku]] (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the [[:en:Kofun period|Kofun period]] in the [[:en:Japanese archipelago|Japanese archipelago]]. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|qq=}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|qq=}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|qq=}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the [[:en:Imperial Household Agency|Imperial Household Agency]] and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or [[:en:Okimi|Great Kings (Yamato court)]]. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in [[:en:Habikino|Habikino]], Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" !
