[[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|WD=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|en|Japanese archipelago|WD=Q841337|lt=Japanese archipelago}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Taichirō Shiraishi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580156}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418120}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Okimi|en|Okimi|WD=Q718995|lt=Great Kings (Yamato court)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|WD=Q694308|lt=Habikino}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|WD=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|en|Japanese archipelago|WD=Q841337|lt=Japanese archipelago}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Taichirō Shiraishi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580156}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418120}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Okimi|en|Okimi|WD=Q718995|lt=Great Kings (Yamato court)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|WD=Q694308|lt=Habikino}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|WD=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|en|Japanese archipelago|WD=Q841337|lt=Japanese archipelago}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Taichirō Shiraishi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580156}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418120}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Okimi|en|Okimi|WD=Q718995|lt=Great Kings (Yamato court)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|WD=Q694308|lt=Habikino}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|WD=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|en|Japanese archipelago|WD=Q841337|lt=Japanese archipelago}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Taichirō Shiraishi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580156}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418120}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Okimi|en|Okimi|WD=Q718995|lt=Great Kings (Yamato court)}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|WD=Q694308|lt=Habikino}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|WD=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku|1=Emperor Nintoku}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|en|Japanese archipelago|WD=Q841337|lt=Japanese archipelago|1=Japanese archipelago}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Shiraishi Taichiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580156}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418120}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Okimi|en|Okimi|WD=Q718995|lt=Great Kings (Yamato court)|1=Okimi}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|WD=Q694308|lt=Habikino|1=Habikino}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|WD=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku|1=Emperor Nintoku}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|en|Japanese archipelago|WD=Q841337|lt=Japanese archipelago|1=Japanese archipelago}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Shiraishi Taichiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580156}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418120}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Okimi|en|Okimi|WD=Q718995|lt=Great Kings (Yamato court)|1=Okimi}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|WD=Q694308|lt=Habikino|1=Habikino}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|WD=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku|1=Emperor Nintoku}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|en|Japanese archipelago|WD=Q841337|lt=Japanese archipelago|1=Japanese archipelago}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Shiraishi Taichiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580156}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418120}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11485567}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Okimi|en|Okimi|WD=Q718995|lt=Great Kings (Yamato court)|1=Okimi}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|WD=Q694308|lt=Habikino|1=Habikino}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|qid=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku|1=Emperor Nintoku}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|en|Japanese archipelago|qid=Q841337|lt=Japanese archipelago|1=Japanese archipelago}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Shiraishi Taichiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11580156}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11418120}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11485567}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Okimi|en|Okimi|qid=Q718995|lt=Great Kings (Yamato court)|1=Okimi}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|qid=Q694308|lt=Habikino|1=Habikino}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|Zenpōkōenfun|en|Zenpōkōenfun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Zenpōkōenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|qid=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku|1=Emperor Nintoku}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|en|Japanese archipelago|qid=Q841337|lt=Japanese archipelago|1=Japanese archipelago}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Shiraishi Taichiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11580156}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11418120}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11485567}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Okimi|en|Okimi|qid=Q718995|lt=Great Kings (Yamato court)|1=Okimi}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|qid=Q694308|lt=Habikino|1=Habikino}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" ! [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[ja:日本の大規模古墳一覧]] [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun|1=Zenpō-kōen-fun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|qid=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku|1=Emperor Nintoku}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|en|Japanese archipelago|qid=Q841337|lt=Japanese archipelago|1=Japanese archipelago}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Shiraishi Taichiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11580156}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11418120}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11485567}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Okimi|en|Okimi|qid=Q718995|lt=Great Kings (Yamato court)|1=Okimi}}. [[File:NintokuTomb Aerial photograph 2007.jpg|thumb|280px|{{ill|Daisenryō Kofun|ja|大仙陵古墳|1=Daisenryō Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Daisenryō Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Japan's largest kofun and a representative example of a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|qid=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun|1=Zenpō-kōen-fun}}. The {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} refers to it as {{ruby|Mozu no Mimihara no Naka no Misazagi|もずのみみはらのなかのみささぎ}} and designates it as the {{ill|Imperial mausoleum|ja|陵墓|1=Japanese imperial tombs|lt=Imperial tomb|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial mausoleum|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese imperial tombs|qq=}} of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|qid=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku|1=Emperor Nintoku}} (alternate name: Nintoku Tennōryō).
Image (taken in 2007)
{{National Land Aerial Photograph}}.]] '''List of Japan's Largest Kofun''' (日本の大規模古墳一覧) is a comprehensive record of large-scale kofun built during the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}} in the {{ill|Japanese archipelago|en|Japanese archipelago|qid=Q841337|lt=Japanese archipelago|1=Japanese archipelago}}. The list is Ranked by tumulus length and includes only kofun with lengths exceeding 200 meters. Additionally, a distribution table by prefecture for kofun over 120 meters in length is included. == List of Large-Scale Kofun Over 200 Meters in Length == The table below is based on the original data of {{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Shiraishi Taichiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11580156}}, supplemented by {{ill|Sui Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sui Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11418120}} (1992){{Sfn|和田萃|1992}} and {{ill|Kazuo Hirose|ja|広瀬和雄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazuo Hirose|1=Kazuo Hirose|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11485567}} (2003){{Sfn|広瀬和雄|2003}}. The designations of imperial mausoleums are by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} and do not necessarily indicate that the associated individuals are actually buried in these kofun. Additionally, the categories of "kofun clusters" or "kofun groups" referenced in the notes largely follow Wada (1992). A total of 37 kofun over 200 meters in length were constructed during the Kofun period in the Japanese archipelago. These are considered the tombs of kings or {{ill|Okimi|en|Okimi|qid=Q718995|lt=Great Kings (Yamato court)|1=Okimi}}. However, the {{ill|Hakayama Kofun|ja|墓山古墳|1=Hakayama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakayama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 23rd), located in {{ill|Habikino|en|Habikino|qid=Q694308|lt=Habikino|1=Habikino}}, Osaka Prefecture, is thought to be a {{ill|baizuka|ja|陪塚|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/baizuka|qq=}} of the nearby {{ill|Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|ja|誉田御廟山古墳|1=Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyōyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Konda Gobyoyama Kofun|qq=}} (Ranked 2nd). {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: right;font-size:small" !
